Reference / web/request

web/request#

The request as an endpoint sees it: route parameters, query, header fields, cookies and a body read under a byte limit.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

async show(request is WebRequest) is Responding {
    let id = request.path().int("id");                       // from "/notes/:id"
    let page = request.query().maybe("page").int() else 1;
    let trace = request.header().maybe("X-Request-Id").text() else "";
    let note = await request.json(65536);
    TextReply("note " + id.string());
}

Description#

The request as an endpoint sees it: route parameters, query, header fields, cookies and a body read under a byte limit.

A client mistake (a bad number, a body too large or of the wrong type) becomes an Exception with the matching status, 400, 413 or 415, naming the value. The body is read once and kept, so an Around and the endpoint can both read it. request() and context() give the std Request and its context.

WebRequest.link#

link(name is string, parameters is ...RouteParameter) is string

The path of a named route with its parameters filled in, percent-encoded (#106): request.link("user", RouteParameter(name: "id", value: "7")) is "/users/7" for Get(path: "/users/:id", endpoint: users.show, name: "user").

WebRequest.parameters#

parameters() is QueryParameters

Query decoded the way browsers and URLSearchParams encode it (application/x-www-form-urlencoded: "+" is a space). The raw RFC 3986 query stays available through request().target().query(). It is decoded once per request, however many parameters an endpoint reads (#75).

WebRequest.bytes#

The body, at most limit bytes; BodyLimitExceeded past it.

WebRequest.text#

async text(limit is int) is string

The body as UTF-8 text, at most limit bytes.

WebRequest.json#

async json(limit is int) is RequestJson

Requires application/json or a +json media type. The document is parsed eagerly, so syntax errors are a 400 here and never escape later as JsonError.invalid; reading errors of the returned RequestJson are 422. The bytes go to the parser as they are (#135): bytes that are not UTF-8 are a 400 that names where they start.

WebRequest.form#

async form(limit is int) is QueryParameters

Requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

role RequestValues#

role RequestValues

Named values a client sent, of one kind: route parameters, query parameters, header fields or cookies. A missing or malformed value is the client's mistake, so the readers throw Exception.status(400, …) naming it, such as "query parameter page must be an integer":

let id = request.path().int("id");
let page = request.query().maybe("page").int() else 1;
let trace = request.header().maybe("X-Request-Id").text() else "";
let session = request.cookies().text("sid");

With a name given more than once, text(), int() and boolean() read the first value and list() all of them; list() of a header field gives the members of its list, and of an absent name [].

WebLinks.link#

link(name is string, parameters is @RouteParameter) is string

The path of the route named name with its parameters filled in. A parameter becomes one percent-encoded segment; a final wildcard keeps its slashes, and an empty one adds nothing. InvalidWebLink for an unknown name, a parameter the pattern lacks, or one it needs and lacks.

object RequestJson#

object RequestJson

The request body as JSON. Same reading API as json.Json, but every reading failure is the client's: it becomes Exception.status(422, …) naming the JSON pointer. Server-side JSON read through a plain Json keeps its own errors, so a bug in server data is never reported to the client as 422.
